tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format. The parser reads the last parseable list, so the move list must be the final content of the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you have generated the full sequence of legal moves for the given Tower of Hanoi instance.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing explanatory text after the move list or outputting the moves earlier in the answer, causing the parser to miss the correct list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A larger disk can only be moved when it is the topmost disk on its peg. If smaller disks sit on top, relocate them to other pegs before attempting to move the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving any disk that is not currently the topmost on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 while disk 2 remains on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk may only be placed on an empty peg or on top of a larger disk. Before executing a move, check that the destination peg satisfies this condition.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Every time you consider moving a disk to a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, which is smaller and therefore illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Only the topmost disk of a peg can be moved. Verify that the disk you intend to move is indeed the current top of its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before performing any move from a source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, which violates the top‑disk rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move n disks from a source peg to a target peg, recursively move n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the n‑1 stack onto the target. This pattern works even when other pegs contain unrelated disks, as long as the recursion respects the current state.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to transfer a clean stack of k disks from one peg to another while the third peg is free to act as auxiliary.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Generating a move list that skips the recursive pattern, leading to missing or extra moves and an incorrect final configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that belong above the larger disk in the final order, move those smaller disks elsewhere first. Only then place the larger disk onto the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to place a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 onto a peg that already has disk 3 on top, which would block the required final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves or forgets to output the move list entirely.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly generate and print the full list of moves; ensure the answer contains at least one move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or ends generation prematurely, leaving the move list unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the answer concise, avoid extra commentary, and ensure the move list fits within the token budget.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving it.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the source peg's top disk and only move that disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to confirm that the destination peg is empty or has a larger top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate the destination peg's top disk (or emptiness) before each move.
